memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it as on a seal: holy to the Lord. Fasten a blue cord to it to attach it to the turban; it is to be on the front of the turban. It will be on Aaron's forehead, and he will bear the guilt involved in the sacred gifts the Israelites consecrate, whatever their gifts may be. It will be on Aaron's forehead continually so that they will be acceptable to the Lord." - Exodus 28:36-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On the front of the turban, right across the forehead, sat a plate of pure gold engraved with three words: holy to the Lord. It was the first thing anyone would see. And its purpose is remarkable — Aaron would "bear the guilt involved in the sacred gifts," so that the people's offerings would be acceptable to God.

Think about what that means. Even Israel's worship was imperfect. Their best gifts, their most sincere offerings, still carried something flawed. So God provided a representative who bore that guilt on their behalf, and the gold plate declared the holiness that made their imperfect worship acceptable.

This is exactly our situation. Our prayers wander. Our worship is mixed with distraction and self-interest. Even our best offerings are stained. But we have a High Priest who bears what is defective in our devotion, and through Him our offerings are made acceptable. Peter writes that we offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ (1 Pet 2:5). You do not need to perfect your worship before bringing it. Bring it through Christ, and He makes it acceptable.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I hold back from worship because I know my heart is not perfectly pure?
How does it free me that Christ makes my imperfect offerings acceptable?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, even my best worship is imperfect, yet through Christ You receive it. Thank You for a High Priest who bears what is flawed in my devotion. I bring You my heart today. Amen.
